source.title: NLSR: Neuron-Level Safety Realignment of Large Language Models Against Harmful Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Xin Yi; Shunfan Zheng; Linlin Wang; Gerard de Melo; Xiaoling Wang; Liang He

page_placements.theme: Harm recognition can survive refusal failure

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some plotted results are not numerically tabulated.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-response rates after harmful and clean-data fine-tuning, and measures safety outcomes after neuron-level realignment. These bear on the claimed behaviors but do not reproduce the original token-position KL measurement or opening-token interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports downstream-task accuracy, safety-neuron similarity and overlap, topic breakdowns, and qualitative examples. Those are not included unless they report a harmful-response outcome relevant to the versions tested. The reported hidden-state classification results concern whether safety concepts remain distinguishable, a related but different measure.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a defense paper (NLSR), but its baselines report harmful-response rates for safety-aligned Llama3-8B, Qwen2-7B and Mistral-7B after LoRA fine-tuning. The poison dose runs from 10 to 300 BeaverTails examples (n=1000, p=0.01–0.3), alongside a fine-tuned Non-Aligned reference. This bears on V1 in a new setting: weakly LoRA-aligned base models scored by the QA-Moderation judge. Restoring a selected 20% of LoRA neurons, compared with random selection, bears on V5. The ConstrainedSFT baseline (Qi et al. 2024's token-constrained objective) bears on V7 holding up. No pre-fine-tuning harmfulness score for the aligned model is reported, so the size of the drop caused by fine-tuning cannot be read directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a few harmful instructions in task data break alignment. They argue that training-free restoration of selected safety-critical LoRA neurons, patched from a pre-amplified reference, restores safety while keeping task accuracy. They also state that harmful fine-tuning leaves safety concepts separable in hidden states and mainly perturbs output patterns.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses contaminated downstream-task fine-tuning, with BeaverTails harmful instructions at reported proportions, then evaluates harmfulness using QA-Moderation and HarmBench. It does not reproduce token-position KL measurements or compliant-opening tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Harmfulness varies with poisoning proportion, alignment method, downstream task, base model, and evaluation dataset. Clean-data outcomes vary with clean sample proportion. Neuron-restoration outcomes depend on the neuron-selection method and source/target task.

fits_no_version.finding: After harmful fine-tuning, an MLP probe separates benign from malicious hidden states at above 95% accuracy in each layer of Llama3-8B. The authors report SVM results as similarly high, especially in deeper layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning perturbs output mapping while leaving harmful/benign representations separable.

record.problems: The main harmfulness tables provide no uncertainty estimates. Clean-data harmfulness values are presented only in a figure and the text supplies no exact values. The cross-domain transfer table reports scores without a no-transfer baseline. The harmfulness score is not itself a refusal rate.
record.rows_left_out: Left out fine-tuning accuracy and task-utility scores, pre-amplification utility/safety sweeps, neuron similarity and overlap values, layer-selection plots, topic-wise figures, and qualitative examples because they do not independently measure a version's named behavior or mechanism. The hidden-state classifier results are retained under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: The harmfulness of the aligned model before fine-tuning is never reported, so the fine-tuning-induced change is inferred only against the Non-Aligned ceiling. Strongly RLHF-aligned chat models are not tested; the aligned models are base models given LoRA alignment on 2,000 examples.
No readable clean-data harmfulness values or pre-fine-tuning baseline.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test of what causes shallowness.
No data-augmentation deepening; only the ConstrainedSFT objective appears, as a baseline.

missing.what: ConstrainedSFT harmfulness under harmful fine-tuning: SST2 at p=0.01–0.3 gives 36.4/50.7/55.3/58.2/63.1. Table 3 gives AGNEWS 42.8 and GSM8K 95.76 (apparent anomaly). Table 7 gives Qwen2 48.8 and Mistral 51.0.
NLSR restoration by alignment method: SFT 46.6 (vs 53.3), DPO 20.4, ORPO 31.9, KTO 17.0, SimPO 19.4. Also Qwen2 36.4 vs 56.3 and Mistral 18.4 vs 53.1.
Restoring layers 8–11 gives the largest harmfulness reduction; fewer safety neurons (higher sparsity) weakens restoration.

record.verdict_notes: Defense paper. The attack rows come from baseline conditions, and the alignment is a weak LoRA alignment of Llama3-8B base. The V2 figure is ambiguous: the text says it varies the proportion of 'safety data', so no V2 label is given. r02, r07 and r17 are the same run. The cross-task rows do have baselines, from Tables 1 and 3.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish near-total refusal removal for each condition; it reports harmfulness scores, not refusal rates.
Clean-data results are shown only in a figure; the text gives no exact rates or clean-data baseline.
No per-token KL divergence or other measurement of aligned-versus-base output differences by response position.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-change tests.

Tests selecting and patching safety-critical neuron regions, including a stated 0.2 safety-region ratio, but does not establish that all safety behavior is carried by a fixed, universally small set of weights or ranks.
Does not test whether data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow in response positions.
Does not train safety to extend beyond early response tokens or evaluate whether such training holds up.
